answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, weighting each signer by the probability that paths from trusted roots reach it. A Sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse cut has low conductance, limiting the probability that these walks enter it. Min-cut transitivity bounds therefore constrain its aggregate voting weight by the cut and walk budget, not its claimed node count, whether its labels are shale, karst, or oasis.
